name: Guardian genius crossword No 213
preamble: The letters in 16 squares are not allowed for in the wordplay of the clues involved. Taken as a group, when encoded these 16 letters magically lead to a number that is to be entered in the box at top of the entry form.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The Queen abandons regular tradition

indicators.note: whoever abandons something walks away from it, so the royal letters leave the word they were in

blocks.note: Elizabeth Regina, the usual crossword queen
a regular at a shop or pub is a customer

explanation.surface: The monarch drops an old habit she has always kept up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular' looks like an adjective for the tradition, but it is a noun: a regular customer, who loses the ER at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is a long-established practice handed down, which is exactly what a tradition is.

clue.text: University a little upset with no good revising

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
one of the sixteen extra letters the preamble says the wordplay ignores
a tad is a little bit
one of the sixteen extra letters the preamble says the wordplay ignores
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A student gets a little upset about a bad mark while revising.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds only U-DAT-NG; the P and I are two of the preamble's sixteen unclued letters, which sit in the unchecked squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Updating something means bringing it up to date by revising it with new information.

clue.text: Heath Robinson component produces deep, rhythmic sound

indicators.note: a component is a part of a larger whole, so the answer is a stretch of the name

blocks.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: A part of one of Heath Robinson's absurd contraptions makes a thumping noise.
explanation.walkthrough: W. Heath Robinson was a British cartoonist famous for drawing ludicrously complicated machines.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a steady, pulsing beat, as of an engine or a heart, a deep rhythmic sound.

clue.text: Procedures might initially get shot to pieces

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter is used
something shot to pieces is broken up, so its letters are scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: the opening letter
one of the sixteen extra letters the preamble says the wordplay ignores
the first three letters of the rearranged word
one of the sixteen extra letters the preamble says the wordplay ignores
the last letter of the rearranged word

explanation.surface: Plans that might go wrong at the first hurdle end up in tatters.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives M plus a jumble of SHOT; the E and D are unclued extras from the preamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Methods are systematic ways of doing things, the same as procedures or techniques.

clue.text: English politician in exam storm

indicators.note: the national tag and the member of parliament sit inside the exam word

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
Member of Parliament
an exam is a test

explanation.surface: An English MP sitting an exam causes uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, as in Shakespeare's play title.

clue.text: Type of seat to build, right on the floor

blocks.note: to erect is to build
one of the sixteen extra letters the preamble says the wordplay ignores
one of the sixteen extra letters the preamble says the wordplay ignores
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Building a seat that sits right on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: ERECT has its R moved to the foot, giving EECTR; the J and O are unclued extras from the preamble.
explanation.definitionFit: An ejector seat is the kind that fires a pilot out of a stricken aircraft.

clue.text: Animal in river to fight back, not with attention

indicators.note: going back means running the fight word the other way
not with means without, so the abbreviation for with is dropped

blocks.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a brawl is a fight
w is the abbreviation for with
to give someone your ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: An animal in a river fights back without anyone paying it attention.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar bear is a large white Arctic animal, a carnivore that hunts seals on the ice.

clue.text: Unkempt person's coats are back-to-front

blocks.note: furs are fur coats

one of the sixteen extra letters the preamble says the wordplay ignores

explanation.surface: A scruffy type has put on his coats inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives only SRUF; the C and F are unclued extras from the preamble.
explanation.definitionFit: A scruff is informal British slang for a person who looks untidy and dishevelled.

clue.text: Carefully move around Spain with captivating lovely borders

indicators.note: to move letters around is to shuffle their order
the borders of a word are its outer edges, first and last letters

blocks.note: the country's letters rearranged
taking means captivating, attractive
its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A careful tour around Spain, enchanted by its lovely frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something painstakingly means taking great care and attention over every detail.

clue.text: Acting school returns for Jewish month

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the school's letters run the other way

blocks.note: the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London

explanation.surface: A drama school breaks up and comes back for a Jewish holiday month.
explanation.definitionFit: Adar is the twelfth month of the Jewish religious calendar, in which Purim falls.

clue.text: Those moving with skill? Reversing learners during turns

indicators.note: reversing a word runs it backwards, applied to the skill word just before it
the learners come during the turns, so they sit in the middle of that word

blocks.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation
two L-plates, one per learner driver
veers means turns aside

explanation.surface: Skilled drivers behind learner cars that keep reversing as they turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark tempts you to read 'Those moving with skill' as the definition, but 'with skill' is wordplay; the travellers are simply those moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Travellers are people on a journey, going from place to place, so they are those moving.

clue.text: Hard to treat end delivered

blocks.note: a stub is the end left over, as of a cigarette
a delivered baby has been born

explanation.surface: Reads like a medical note: a condition hard to treat, ending in delivery of a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn ailments or stains resist every remedy, so they are difficult to treat or shift.

clue.text: Afrit cryptic following 1s

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling and hidden, so the demon's name is jumbled

blocks.note: an afrit is a demon of Arabian myth, used as written
f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A puzzling Arabian demon follows the customs of the first clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 1s points to 1 across, CUSTOM, made plural: customs are the duties charged on goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a tax or duty levied on imports, which is what customs payments are.

clue.text: Allegedly wants massages

indicators.note: allegedly means as people say, so the word goes by its spoken form

blocks.note: wants in the sense of requires

explanation.surface: Someone supposedly needs a massage.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading is working muscles with the hands, the core action of a massage therapist.

clue.text: Rider preparing for trade week?

indicators.note: preparing means putting together or making ready, so these letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A jockey gets ready for a busy week of business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' suggests a horseman, but it is the definition in its other sense: an addition to a document.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an added clause or note at the end of a document, and an afterword is a closing section of a book.

clue.text: Jailor frees northern bird

blocks.note: an old word for a jailer, who turns the key
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A prison guard releases a northern bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The turkey is a large farmyard fowl, a familiar game and table bird.

blocks.note: a pig of a job is a very hard one

what pupils call a male teacher
one of the sixteen extra letters the preamble says the wordplay ignores

explanation.definitionFit: Pilgrims are people who journey to a holy place, so they are a kind of traveller.

clue.text: Hit by small vehicle …

a truck is a goods vehicle

explanation.surface: Someone knocked down by a little van, the ellipsis carrying the story into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Struck is the past tense of strike, meaning hit or knocked.

clue.text: Wretched posh girl

blocks.note: U for upper-class, the old label for posh usage

the first three letters of the girl's name Lucy
one of the sixteen extra letters the preamble says the wordplay ignores
the last letter of the name

explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives only U and LUCY; the N and K are unclued extras from the preamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Wretched can mean ill-fated, and an unlucky person is one dogged by misfortune.

clue.text: … and another tug?

blocks.note: the ellipsis carries over 'small' from the clue above, giving the same abbreviation again
another vehicle, following on from the truck

explanation.surface: Continuing the accident story: hit by another vehicle, a tugboat perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue leans on 18 across: 'and another' means small plus another vehicle. 'Tug' looks like a boat but is the definition, a pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a hard pull or tug on something, as when you strain at a rope.

clue.text: State of meditation is uplifting to suppress being angry

indicators.note: lifting up in a down clue makes the little word read from bottom to top
to suppress is to hold down, keeping the anger word inside

blocks.note: taken as written
one of the sixteen extra letters the preamble says the wordplay ignores
mad means angry
one of the sixteen extra letters the preamble says the wordplay ignores

explanation.surface: Meditation lifts the spirits and keeps anger in check.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives S-MAD-I; the A and H are unclued extras from the preamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Samadhi is the Hindu and Buddhist term for the deepest state of meditative concentration.

clue.text: Extremists drain contents of espresso at summerhouse

first and last letters

explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a small open garden pavilion, a summerhouse for sitting out in fine weather.

clue.text: Guard in Lord of the Rings, perhaps, assists leaders in trouble

blocks.clueFragment: Lord of the Rings, perhaps, assists
blocks.note: the first letter of each of the six words

explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' after Guard reads as part of the definition, but it belongs with 'trouble' to signal the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrol is a group of soldiers or police keeping watch over an area, so it guards it.

clue.text: Science of law: no money for a quiet defence

taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawyer offers no fee to mount a quiet defence.
explanation.walkthrough: Apology here is the old sense of a reasoned defence, as in Plato's Apology of Socrates, not an expression of regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomology is the study of laws, from Greek nomos meaning law, so it is a science of law.
